capabilities.target: Paid third-party enrichment API call, billed per call against a shared monthly quota
Spawn a sub-agent to research an account; sub-agents can themselves spawn further researchers
CRM account fields: industry, size, headquarters

inputs.source: Nightly batch of CRM account rows (40,000 rows) queued for enrichment

instructions.note: "If a lookup fails or looks incomplete" gives no objective, checkable criterion for when to retry versus spawn a researcher sub-agent.
"Keep going until every row is complete" has no retry cap, step cap, or timeout, and roughly 3 percent of the 40,000-row batch can never reach 'complete' because the company name is malformed.
The only boundary on spend, retries, and sub-agent spawning is the prompt's wording. Runtime notes confirm no structural step, runtime, retry, or spawn limit exists anywhere in the design.

elements.name: Shared enrichment API key and monthly quota

controls.name: Maximum unattended steps / runtime limit for the nightly batch run
controls.decay_rationale: Not implemented. Runtime notes state there is no maximum on steps or runtime. If enforced by the orchestrator rather than the model, this would not decay with model capability.

controls.name: Sub-agent spawn depth and count limit
controls.decay_rationale: Not implemented. Runtime notes state sub-agents can spawn their own researchers with no limit.

controls.name: Spend alert and automatic circuit breaker on enrichment API usage
controls.decay_rationale: Not implemented. Runtime notes explicitly state there is no spend alert on the enrichment account.

controls.name: Dedicated enrichment API quota/key, isolated from sales and marketing
controls.decay_rationale: Not implemented. Runtime notes state the API key and monthly quota are shared with the sales and marketing teams.

controls.name: Objective per-row retry/completion cap with human review fallback
controls.decay_rationale: Not implemented. The prompt only instructs the model to keep retrying or spawning until complete (behavioral, dependent), with no structural bound and no fallback to human review for rows that never complete.

findings.title: Unbounded retry/spawn loop on malformed rows drains shared enrichment quota (spend-loop pattern, TC6 variant) — denial of service for sales and marketing

attack_path.note: 40,000-row nightly batch; ~3% of rows have malformed company names that never resolve
Retried indefinitely per row with no retry cap, billed per call against the shared quota
Recursive sub-agent spawning on ambiguous 'looks incomplete' rows multiplies enrich.lookup calls with no depth or count limit
Shared monthly quota exhausted; sales and marketing tools stop working until next month

forecast.watch_signal: Monthly enrichment spend as a percentage of shared quota; number of sales/marketing tool-access failures attributed to quota exhaustion; peak concurrent spawned researcher sub-agents per nightly run; batch size growth beyond 40,000 rows.

evidence.observation: Instruction says to retry or spawn a researcher sub-agent and 'keep going until every row is complete,' with no stated termination bound.
There is no maximum on steps, runtime, retries, or sub-agents. Sub-agents can spawn their own researchers.
enrich.lookup is billed per call; the API key and monthly quota are shared with the sales and marketing teams, and when the quota runs out their tools stop working until the next month.
Roughly 3 percent of the 40,000-row nightly batch have malformed company names that never return a complete result, guaranteeing repeated retries and spawns every single night.
There is no spend alert on the enrichment account.

recommendations.action: Add a hard cap on unattended steps, runtime minutes, retries per row, and sub-agent spawn depth/count for the nightly enrichment run, enforced by the orchestrator rather than by prompt instruction.

Give the enrichment agent a dedicated API key and quota isolated from the shared sales/marketing quota, and add a spend alert with an automatic circuit breaker that halts the batch before the quota is exhausted.
Add real-time spend and quota-consumption monitoring with alerting well before exhaustion, visible to the teams sharing the quota.

findings.title: Unvalidated CRM writes from an ambiguous completion criterion (no data-quality gate before write)

attack_path.note: Ambiguous 'looks incomplete' criterion (prompt.md:2) drives retries/spawns with no objective quality bar
Recursively spawned researchers investigate ambiguous or malformed accounts and may produce speculative results
Writes industry/size/headquarters fields with no stated validation or confidence gate before committing to CRM

forecast.watch_signal: Rate of CRM field corrections/reverts on enrichment-written rows; growth in average sub-agent recursion depth per row; batch size or data-source growth feeding in.crm_rows.

evidence.observation: 'If a lookup fails or looks incomplete, retry, or spawn a researcher sub agent' gives no objective completeness criterion and no mention of a validation step before the result is written to CRM.
The agent is instructed to fill in industry, size, and headquarters directly via enrich.lookup, with no mention of a review or confidence check before cap.crm_write.

No step, runtime, retry, or spawn limits exist, so recursively spawned researchers investigating ambiguous accounts can produce speculative or low-confidence data that is still eligible to be written to CRM.

recommendations.action: Replace the ambiguous 'keep going until complete' instruction with a bounded, objective completion rule (for example, at most 2 retries, then mark the row 'needs_review') and route rows that still fail to human review instead of indefinite sub-agent spawning.
Add a validation or confidence gate before cap.crm_write commits fields, especially for rows resolved through recursive sub-agent delegation.

rating.rationale: Both findings stem from a fully autonomous batch agent (A4, no step/runtime/retry/spawn limits, can recursively spawn sub-agents) acting on internal CRM data with zero declared or verified guardrails. Finding f1's sink (billed API calls against a shared monthly quota, and recursive delegation) scores as action:spend/delegate, which is automatically S3; combined with an internal-trust source and the A4 autonomy modifier, inherent reaches critical, and the deterministic 3-percent malformed-row rate makes this reachable on an ordinary night, not only under attack. Finding f2's write sink is S2, giving inherent high under the same autonomy modifier. All five recommended controls (step/runtime cap, spawn-depth cap, spend alert/circuit breaker, quota isolation, bounded retry/review fallback) are absent (status missing_recommended), so no rubric credit applies anywhere and residual equals inherent for both findings. Because f1 already sits at the ceiling tier, no forecast trigger can raise it further; forecast equals residual for both findings. The gap this assessment flags is not control decay but control absence: the single highest-leverage fix is ctl.quota_isolation plus ctl.spend_cap, since those two together sever the cross-team denial-of-service consequence even if the retry/spawn loop itself is not yet bounded.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided artifacts (prompt.md and runtime notes), not observed runtime behavior.

No MCP/tool manifest, IaC, or orchestrator configuration was provided; capability scope, credential scope, and the absence of spend alerts or step/spawn limits are inferred from the prompt and runtime notes text, so confidence on exact mechanism details is capped at medium where not explicitly stated.

No approval, logging, or monitoring configuration was described in the artifacts; their absence is taken at face value from the runtime notes, which explicitly state there is no spend alert and no step/retry/spawn limits.
